newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN says airlift to refugees in east Zaire imminent.
newsitem.headline: UN says airlift to refugees in east Zaire imminent.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency said on Tuesday that it would start airlifting relief supplies in the coming days to hundreds of thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees fleeing Tutsi rebels in eastern Zaire.

Spokeswoman Ruth Marshall told a briefing that supplies would be flown from Zaire's capital Kinshasa to Kisangani, the last outpost of tenuous Zairean authority before a wilderness of forest and hills. The town is 500 km (310 miles) from eastern Zaire's volatile border region of Goma.
Supplies would then be trucked from Kisangani to the refugees -- with whom the UNHCR has lost contact since fighting broke out three weeks ago.
More than half a million mostly Rwandan Hutu refugees fled their camps outside Rwanda's borders after Rwandan-backed Tutsi Banyamulenge rebels seized large swathes of eastern Zaire.
"We're trying from every direction that we can to get aid effectively and quickly to all the people in need -- refugees and displaced Zaireans," Marshall said.
Marshall said UNHCR had no evidence of a mass exodus of refugees from eastern Zaire's Goma region on Rwanda's northwestern border to Kisangani.

The main road from Goma and Bukavu to Kisangani was used as a line of retreat for troops from the battlefront. Recent aid flights over the area have revealed few people on the road, but also that the villages were deserted.

The United Nations said in Geneva that 40 tonnes of high energy biscuits had been airlifted to Uganda's capital Kampala. Another 100 tonnes of relief supplies would be flown to Kinshasa from Denmark on Wednesday on board a Russian Antonov 124 plane.
